text:
maya: FYI customer ACME (ticket #87122) reports a sudden token spike in their invoice — 32k extra tokens for a ~5k request volume window.
jane_acme: Confirmed — we saw a bill jump around 2025-09-14T18:12Z. Dashboard show normal request counts but invoice shows more tokens. I can share example request ids.
maya: Can you paste one full request/response with headers? suspect retries or missing idempotency keys.
jane_acme: Here you go:
- request id: req_8f9a123
- curl snippet:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Idempotency-Key: " -d '{"messages": [{"role":"user","content":"summarize..."}], "max_tokens":512 }'
```
(note: their SDK currently doesn't set idempotency for chat calls)
samir: ops-bot shows gateway 504 at 18:11:57Z for region us-west-2, followed by a cluster of retries from acme-proxy for that client IP.
ops-bot: incident: gateway_timeout 504 -> retried 3x for client req_8f9a123 window (18:11:57 - 18:12:03).
ryan: If SDK didn't set idempotency key, our gateway retry logic will forward each replay as a distinct ingest event -> double/triple token accounting unless client dedupes on our ledger.
liya: We track token usage at ingest boundary and increment ledger per ingestion. Retries that re-ingest will produce extra token rows unless the ingestion provides an idempotency key we can match.
maya: So hypothesis: proxy retried because of 504, SDK re-sent without idempotency header -> multiple ingests -> billed multiple times. Need to verify ledger rows around that timestamp.
samir: I queried the ingest ledger table for req_8f9a123 window:
```
SELECT ingest_id, received_at, client_ip, idempotency_key FROM ingest_ledger
WHERE client_ip='52.7.11.33' AND received_at BETWEEN '2025-09-14 18:11:50' AND '2025-09-14 18:12:10';
```
Result: 3 rows, idempotency_key NULL for all. ingest_ids: ing_901, ing_902, ing_903.
liya: Billing entries: three usage rows linked to those ingest_ids each counted ~10.8k tokens -> total ~32.4k. Matches invoice delta.
jane_acme: Their SDK sends no idempotency header for streaming/chat prior to v1.4.0, they upgraded later but these calls came from an older SDK pinned in their app.
ryan: Repro steps for devs: simulate 504 at gateway, auto-retry from reverse proxy (we use haproxy at client edge) without idempotency -> expect 3 ledger rows. test snippet:
```
# simulate
for i in 1 2 3; do curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat || true; sleep 0.5; done
```
Check ingest_ledger and billing_ledger counts.
samir: Short-term mitigation: add defensive dedupe on ledger ingestion to look at (client_ip, request_body_hash, timestamp_window) for NULL idempotency_key to collapse likely replays. I can prototype a 5s de-dupe window.
liya: Agree, but we need to be careful not to undercount legitimate distinct requests. Make it opt-in and flag suspicious merges for audit.
maya: Customer wants immediate credit for the duplicated tokens. Can billing issue a pro-rated refund while we implement mitigations?
liya: We'll issue a one-time invoice adjustment for ACME for the duplicate events. Need clear audit trail: list ingest_ids to reverse: ing_901, ing_902, ing_903. I'll open a refund PR and CC finance.
jane_acme: Thanks. Also we'll inventory SDK versions internally and push upgrade to v1.4.0 to ensure future calls set `Idempotency-Key`.
ryan: Long term: SDK should set idempotency by default for chat/generate calls that are safe to replay, and gateway should prefer returning a 202+status that is easier for clients to surface.
samir: I'll sketch implementation: 1) add short-lived server-side dedupe (configurable) 2) add telemetry flag when ingestion arrives without idempotency_key but with rapid repeats 3) create billing-safe rollback path.
maya: Can someone add a short doc/snippet to support playbook so agents can triage quickly? e.g. how to run the ingest_ledger query, how to identify repeated ingests, and refund steps.
ryan: I'll draft the playbook doc and ping you all in #devex when ready. includes standard queries and `--explain` examples.
liya: Refund action taken: adjusted invoice 87122 by -$12.45 to offset 2 duplicate ingests (ref #REF-2025-218). Customer notified.
jane_acme: Received refund notice, thank you — we'll roll SDK update by end of week.
maya: Closing loop: create follow-up ticket to instrument gateway retries and ensure idempotency header propagation. Assign to @samir. :white_check_mark:
samir: Got it, created internal task INF-3327. ETA for prototype: 3 days.
maya: Thanks team. Thread closed for now — reopen if any discrepancy reappears.
